To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The transmucosal PD is a function of the nutrient ion concentrations of K+, Na+ and Cl-.
the increase of K+ conductivity is smaller than the increase of NaCl symport conductivity and that HCO3- conductivity increases with inhibition of secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the gastric mucosa.
the regulation of ion transport in the frog stomach.
the effects of changes in the nutrient ion concentration on the transmugosal PD and on the resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the resting fundus of the frog stomach, the transmucosa conductance is dominated by the NaCl symporter and that the increase in HCO3- permeability is the major factor in the increase in conductances in going from the secreting state to the resting state.
the conductance changes for K+ and HCO3- in the resting fundus are much smaller than those in the secreting state, while the changes in the conductance of the Cl- symport pathway are similar.

in the secreting stomach, the increase in K+ conductance is lower than the increase of HCO3- and NaCl symport pathways, and that in the resting stomach, the increase is lower than the sum of the increase in HCO3- symport pathway and NaCl symporter pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NaCl symporter pathway and HCO3- pathways were the major pathways for acid secretion and that K+ conductance was the major pathway for the resting membrane potential.
the increase of HCO3- and NaCl conductance in the resting stomach is the main cause for the increase of PD.
in the fundic mucosa the NaCl symporter is the major conductance pathway in the resting stomach and that in the secreting stomach it is the K+ conductance that is the major conductive pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the changes in delta PD with changes in nutrient ion concentrations can be used as a measure of the changes in the conductances of the ion pathways.
the conductance of the Cl- pathway is the same in secreting and in resting fundi, but the conductance of NaCl symport is higher in resting fundus than in secreting fundi.
the changes in nutrient ion concentrations are not the only factors determining the magnitude of the PD.
